facts.statement: Palaeontologist Augusto Tapia discovered the holotype of the genus in 1918.
facts.quote: In 1918, palaeontologist Augusto Tapia (1893–1966) discovered the genus holotype.

facts.statement: Tapia named the type species N. bonarellii in 1918.
facts.quote: He also named the type species, N. bonarellii (originally spelt as Notoceratops Bonarelli), in 1918.

facts.statement: The generic name is derived from the Greek words notos (south), keras (horn), and ops (face).
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek notos, "the south", keras, "horn" and ops, "face".

facts.statement: The specific name honors Guido Bonarelli, who advised Tapia on the study of the find.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Guido Bonarelli (1871-1951), who advised Tapia in his study of the find.

facts.statement: The fossil found near Lago Colhué Huapi in Chubut was described by Friedrich von Huene in 1929 but has since been lost.
facts.quote: The fossil, found near the Lago Colhué Huapi in Chubut, was eventually described by Friedrich von Huene in 1929, but it has since been lost.

facts.statement: Initially classified as a putative ceratopsian, the lost holotype prevents confident classification, with some researchers suggesting it belongs to a hadrosaur instead.
facts.quote: Initially classified as a putative ceratopsian found in the Lago Colhué Huapi Formation, the lost fragmentary holotype precludes confident referral of this taxon within ornithischians, with some researchers suggesting that it belongs to a hadrosaur instead.

facts.statement: The 2003 discovery of Serendipaceratops from Australia could potentially change the view that Notoceratops is not a ceratopsian.
facts.quote: However, the 2003 discovery of another possible ceratopsian, Serendipaceratops, from Australia could change this view.

facts.statement: An analysis by Tom Rich et al. (2014) concluded that the holotype of Notoceratops had ceratopsian features.
facts.quote: An analysis published by Tom Rich et al. (2014), which focused on the validity of Serendipaceratops, also examined the published material from Notoceratops and concluded that the holotype had ceratopsian features.

facts.statement: The genus is considered a dubious taxon (nomen dubium).
facts.quote: genus: Notoceratops dudoso

facts.statement: The species was described in 1918 by Argentine paleontologist Augusto Tapia from an incomplete dentary bone found in Chubut province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Fue descrito en 1918 por el paleontólogo argentino Augusto Tapia a partir de un hueso dentario incompleto hallado en la provincia de Chubut, Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype, an incomplete and toothless left dentary, was found in Late Cretaceous sediments near Lago Colhué Huapi in the Bajo Barreal Formation, Chubut, Patagonia.
facts.quote: El holotipo, un dentario izquierdo incompleto y sin dientes, fue encontrado en sedimentos del Cretácico Superior cerca del lago Colhué Huapi, en la Formación Bajo Barreal (Miembro Superior), provincia de Chubut, Patagonia.

facts.statement: Tapia named the species in honor of geologist Guido Bonarelli, who collaborated on the study of the fossil.
facts.quote: Tapia denominó la especie en honor al geólogo Guido Bonarelli, quien colaboró en el estudio del fósil.

facts.statement: The type specimen, originally described by Tapia and reillustrated by von Huene (1929), consists of the anterior portion of a dentary with empty alveoli.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo, descrito originalmente por Tapia y reilustrado por von Huene (1929), consiste en la porción anterior de un dentario con alveolos vacíos.

facts.statement: Paleontologist José Bonaparte indicated that the fossil was transferred in 1988 to the Natural Sciences Museum of the National University of San Juan.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el paleontólogo José Bonaparte indicó que el fósil había sido transferido en 1988 al Museo de Ciencias Naturales de la Universidad Nacional de San Juan.

facts.statement: The current location of the fossil remains uncertain, but published illustrations serve as the official diagnostic reference.
facts.quote: Su ubicación actual sigue siendo incierta, pero las ilustraciones publicadas funcionan como referencia diagnóstica oficial.

facts.statement: Tapia originally classified Notoceratops as a ceratopsian based on jaw shape, including an oblique dental row and a gradually elevated coronoid process, features von Huene also considered close to Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Tapia clasificó originalmente a Notoceratops como un ceratopsiano, basándose en la forma de la mandíbula, con una fila dental oblicua y un proceso coronoideo gradualmente elevado, rasgos que von Huene también consideró afines a Ceratopsidae.

facts.statement: Ralph E. Molnar (1980) suggested the specimen corresponded to a hadrosaurid based on its biogeographic context and the absence of other ceratopsians in Gondwana.
facts.quote: Ralph E. Molnar (1980) sugirió que el ejemplar correspondía a un hadrosáurido basándose en su contexto biogeográfico y la ausencia de otros ceratopsianos en Gondwana.

facts.statement: José Bonaparte (1986) provisionally included it in Protoceratopsidae, though he later reconsidered this assignment.
facts.quote: José Bonaparte (1986) lo incluyó provisionalmente en Protoceratopsidae, aunque más tarde reconsideró esa asignación.

facts.statement: Coria and Cambiaso (2007) proposed it might belong to a basal ornithopod, while Ibiricu et al. (2010) suggested affinities with the South American hadrosaur Secernosaurus koerneri found in the same formation.
facts.quote: Coria y Cambiaso (2007) propusieron que podría pertenecer a un ornitópodo basal, mientras que Ibiricu et al. (2010) sugirieron afinidades con el hadrosaurio sudamericano Secernosaurus koerneri, hallado en la misma formación.

facts.statement: Authors reinterpreted von Huene's illustrations and found several diagnostic traits of Ceratopsia: an oblique dental margin, robust symphysis, and a gently elevated coronoid process.
facts.quote: Los autores reinterpretaron las ilustraciones de von Huene y hallaron varios rasgos diagnósticos propios de Ceratopsia: margen dental oblicuo, sínfisis robusta y proceso coronoideo suavemente elevado.

facts.statement: They concluded that both Tapia and von Huene likely correctly identified the fossil as a ceratopsian, and its existence in Gondwana cannot be ruled out.
facts.quote: Concluyeron que tanto Tapia como von Huene probablemente identificaron correctamente el fósil como un ceratopsiano, y que su existencia en Gondwana no puede descartarse.

facts.statement: It represents the first attempt to recognize a ceratopsian in the southern hemisphere, decades before Serendipaceratops was known in Australia.
facts.quote: Representa el primer intento de reconocer un ceratopsiano en el hemisferio sur, décadas antes de que se conociera Serendipaceratops en Australia.

facts.statement: The time range is the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Notoceratops is a dubious genus of extinct ornithischian dinosaur meaning "southern horned face".
rejected.quote: Notoceratops (meaning "southern horned face") is a dubious genus of extinct ornithischian dinosaur.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is a dubious genus of extinct ornithischian dinosaur'

rejected.statement: The genus was described based on an incomplete, toothless left dentary from the Late Cretaceous of Patagonia, Argentina, likely dating to the Campanian or Maastrichtian.
rejected.quote: The genus was described based on an incomplete, toothless left dentary (now lost) from the Late Cretaceous of Patagonia (in Argentina), probably dating to the Campanian or Maastrichtian.
